relevance.rationale: Could not read it. The document is a 26-page seminar-proceedings survey on L^2-torsion of 3-manifolds whose narrative is in Japanese; the PDF embeds an Adobe-Japan1 font with no available mapping, so pdftotext (poppler 24.02.0) and all five rungs of scripts/pdf-extract.py recover only the LaTeX-escaped formula fragments and the Latin-script bibliography. What IS legible: the Fuglede-Kadison determinant definition (including the explicit log-series formula and the norm bound K >= ||R_B||_inf), the L^2-Betti number b(B), an L^2-Reidemeister vs L^2-analytic torsion comparison, section headings for an S^1-case, one 'Conjecture' line adjacent to a 'Volume' fragment, and bibliography entries pointing at L^2-torsion of hyperbolic manifolds of finite volume. That is enough to identify the topic but not enough to state a theorem or judge which, if any, statement the folio could use. The corpus's torsion usage is adjoint/twisted Reidemeister torsion (the 1-loop = torsion cluster: garoufalidis-yoon, pandey-wong, ohtsuki-takata, dimofte-garoufalidis) and Neumann-Zagier; grep finds no L^2-torsion, no Fuglede-Kadison and no Luck-Schick anywhere in content/, computations/ or docs/. So no consumer is visible from the readable fragments, but I am recording undetermined rather than tangential because the judgement turns on statements I could not read.

proposedActions.rationale: Nothing can be proposed against an unreadable body. If the folio wants this line of work, the productive step is obtaining an English-language source for the same material (or an OCR pass with a Japanese language pack) rather than re-triaging this file; a re-upload changes source_sha and re-opens the row.
